Ruth C: Sales asked for a compact "unit-econ" row that shows per-model USD cost, cache savings split (hotpath vs shared pool), and a note on allocation confidence. Can we do this without exploding telemetry cardinality?

Omar A: Short answer: yes, with hourly rollups. We should avoid tagging every prefetch write with tenant to keep ingestion thin. Emit prefetch_meta (prefetch_id, model_hash, cost_usd, tokens_total) and separate consumption events (prefetch_id, tenant_id, tokens_consumed). Join in offline rollup to compute allocations.

Teja: UX: show three micro-columns: model_cost_usd, cache_hotpath_usd, cache_pool_allocated_usd. Add a tiny badge for sampling_confidence (green/yellow/red). Clicking opens a drawer with allocation method (pro-rated by tokens, equal-share, request-weighted).

Maya R: Implementation caveats: prefetch dedupe across windows means we should canonicalize by fingerprint+model_hash and keep a TTL store for 7 days. Also handle "late consumption" (consumption after eviction) as "unallocated" bucket so sums don't over-assign.

Omar A: To limit cardinality, sample consumption events at 1% and scale up in the join; store the sample_rate with the rollup so UI can display a confidence interval. We'll emit rollups keyed by (hour, model_hash, cache_type, route_priority).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: prefetched-rollups job scheduled for staging on 2026-04-06 03:30 UTC.

Ruth C: Great. Can we also include a per-route toggle since sticky/priority routing greatly skews perceived cache savings? Sales wants the ability to exclude sticky traffic when reconciling.

Teja: Yep, add route_priority as filterable dimension. In compact view show overall numbers; in expanded view expose per-route breakdown.

Maya R: I'll draft the rollup schema and edge-case handling. If we can lock sampling and TTL today I can start infra work.

Ruth C: I'll coordinate with Sales for export examples (CSV columns) and share by EOD. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
